rationale: Expected abstain and the bot returned insufficient, clearly stating the docs don't cover it. It is polite and offers a person from the support team.
The expected behavior is answer (WordPress admin exclusion, Shields, adblockers), but the bot abstained. The status does not match the expected behavior.

It correctly says to open a Paddle invoice and click Add address & VAT Number, and that details apply from then on, with every claim supported. Since the customer already paid, it should have said explicitly that invoices already issued stay as they were, and it omits the VAT effects.

It correctly states the limit of 30 IP addresses per website, which the evidence supports. It doesn't address the customer's 40 addresses or mention that IP ranges aren't supported and each full address must be added one at a time.
It correctly says billing is based on total usage across all sites in a team, which resolves the per-site versus total question. Omitting that each team is billed separately is non-essential here.
It explains that old bookmarked links stop working and gives the new root URL, both supported by the evidence. It omits only the non-essential note that there is no automatic redirect.
Expected abstain and the bot returned insufficient without guessing. It is polite and offers a person from the support team, though it doesn't explicitly steer back to Plausible topics.
It gives all four de-duplication strategies (history.replaceState, callback, server-side age check, marking orders), each taken directly from the evidence. It fully resolves the question.

It correctly explains that without a custom event filter the tab includes pageviews that lack the property, and it adds the null/undefined and partial-sending causes. Every claim is supported by the cited evidence.
It gives the Site Search custom event snippet with the search_term prop and says to add the goal, all supported by the evidence. It omits only the non-essential billing note.
